details:
## Impact

An authenticated user who can run Valkey JSON mutating commands can use a
recursive JSONPath expression to make the module free a JSON value that is
still held in the result set being iterated, and then write through the
dangling pointer. This reliably crashes the server process, and has been
developed into remote code execution running as the user the server runs as.

This issue affects the Valkey JSON module in all released versions (1.0.0,
1.0.1 and 1.0.2), including the valkey-bundle distributions that ship it. A
server that does not load the JSON module is not affected.

## Details

`Selector::eval` in `src/json/selector.cc` records each JSONPath match as a
raw `JValue *`. `getUniqueResultSet` deduplicates those matches by pointer,
but it does not eliminate ancestor/descendant overlap and does not stabilize
the pointers. A recursive path such as `$..*` therefore returns both a
parent array and the elements nested inside it.

The size-changing mutators in `src/json/dom.cc` walk that result set in
document order, so the ancestor is mutated first. RapidJSON's
`Reserve()`/`PushBack()` reallocates the parent's element buffer and frees
the old storage, after which the descendant entries still in the result set
point into freed memory. The loop then dereferences and writes through them.
`JSON.ARRAPPEND`, `JSON.ARRINSERT`, `JSON.ARRPOP`, `JSON.ARRTRIM` and
`JSON.CLEAR` all share this pattern. `JSON.CLEAR` additionally reaches a
second destruction path, where it can free storage the ancestor's clear has
already released.

Because the freed chunk is a small ordinary heap allocation, it can be
reclaimed with attacker-controlled bytes and shaped into a counterfeit array
header, which turns the stale write into a write to an attacker-selected
address. This was used to overwrite the module's allocator callback and
obtain native code execution on an official valkey-bundle image.

The fix orders matched nodes deepest-first so a parent's element buffer is
never reallocated before its descendants have been consumed, and rewrites
the array mutators to write their results by index into a pre-sized vector
so replies stay in document order.

## Mitigation

You can mitigate this issue by using Valkey ACLs to restrict the Valkey JSON
mutating commands, in particular `JSON.ARRAPPEND`, `JSON.ARRINSERT`,
`JSON.ARRPOP`, `JSON.ARRTRIM` and `JSON.CLEAR`, if your application does not
intend to use them. Applications that pass user-controlled JSONPath
expressions to those commands are the most exposed; confining paths to
non-recursive expressions also avoids the defect.

## Credits

The defect was independently reported by Joao Teles, by Pham Huong Giang,
by Troy Coll: [troy.coll@salesforce.com](mailto:troy.coll@salesforce.com) of Heroku Data Services (Salesforce), 
who reported it through Aiven's vulnerability disclosure program. Joao Teles reported it first and
supplied the full exploitation chain. 
The fix was authored by https://github.com/zackcam.
